newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Germany's Kohl in Canberra for talks with Howard.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kohl in Canberra for talks with Howard.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl arrived in Canberra on Sunday ahead of a day of talks with Australian political leaders.
Kohl, 67, the West's longest-serving leader, flew into the Australian capital with a delegation of senior business people after a weekend break in tropical Queensland state.
Kohl was welcomed at the Fairbairn air force base in Canberra by Australian Prime Minister John Howard.
While there will be no burning bilateral issues to discuss, Monday's talks will be an opportunity to review and strengthen trade and diplomatic ties between the two nations.
Kohl will on Monday visit Australia's War Memorial and the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier before talks with Howard. The two leaders will give a joint news conference with Howard at 12 p.m (0200 GMT).
Kohl, who arrived in Australia on Friday for a five-day visit, had a first-hand look at one of the world's natural wonders on Saturday when he went swimming on the Great Barrier Reef.
Australian officials have been hoping to use Kohl's visit to encourage tourism from Germany -- Germans spend more per head in Australia than any other foreign visitors.
